transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-06-23 16:00 PDT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Liam Patel (Redwood SE); Sofia Alvarez (NovaPay - Lead ML Eng); Ethan Park (NovaPay - Infra); Priya Menon (NovaPay - CTO)
Links shared: perf deck https://redwood.app/decks/novapay-throughput, benchmark sheet /drive/novapay-perf.xlsx, SOC2 summary (link sent after)

Summary: quick sync on throughput tuning: continuous batching, concurrency targets, queueing/backpressure, and next steps for 4-hour run.

[00:00] Maya: All right everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call - we got Sofia, Ethan, Priya from NovaPay, and Liam and I from Redwood. Is that correct?
[00:10] Sofia: yep that's right, uh hi all.
[00:12] Ethan: hi, thanks.
[00:20] Maya: Cool. Agenda - quick run through of last week's numbers, what we changed on batching, then plan for the 4-hour benchmark and any infra asks.

[00:35] Liam: Cool, I'll kick off with the numbers. last week we saw average throughput of ~1.2k reqs per second on your test cluster with the initial batching config. p95 latency was around 320ms which was a bit high for your SLOs. We tuned continuous batching and dropped p95 to ~180ms while increasing throughput to about 1.9k rps.
[01:05] Sofia: when you say continuous batching, can you just re-iterate what you changed? we sort of saw some spikes.
[01:12] Liam: sure. so originally the batch windows were conservative - we were waiting up to 80ms for a fill. we adjusted to an adaptive window with target batch_size=12-24 and enabled the low-latency flush on p50 timeouts, also turned on prefix KV caching for repeated prompts which cut token generation time by ~8-12% for some flows.
[01:42] Priya: KV cash? do you mean KV cache? (laughs)
[01:45] Liam: yes kv cache, sorry, my bad.

[02:00] Ethan: on the infra side we saw queue depth climb during peak - what's the recommendation for concurrency caps vs autoscale?
[02:08] Liam: good question. We recommend a two-pronged approach: cap concurrency per worker to avoid tail latency amplification (we used cap=32 in tests), but set autoscale policies to add pods on sustained queue depth above threshold. that avoids head-of-line blocking. Also enable request queueing with a short TTL (we set 6s) so short bursts don't trigger scale up immediately.
[02:40] Sofia: That TTL felt a little arbitrary - how do you decide 6s?
[02:44] Liam: empirically - we look at your request pattern. your 24h traces earlier showed ~75% of bursts sub-3s; a 6s TTL lets the queue smooth and batching increase, while still dropping really long waits. We'll verify with the 4-hour run.

[03:10] Maya: quick note on costs - continuous batching gives better throughput/unit-cost but can increase p50 a bit. tradeoff is p95 vs cost. you had asked for concurrency target to hit 3k rps, right?
[03:23] Sofia: correct, target is 3k rps sustained for our peak windows.
[03:27] Liam: to hit 3k we estimate you need Dedicated capacity with 4x A100-equivalent workers or equivalent quantized model variants. one alternative is higher batch sizes with low precision (4-bit) quant which reduces memory footprint and increases throughput but there's a small quality/regression risk.
[03:50] Priya: can you quantify the risk? we run some payment intent summarization so errors are sensitive.
[03:55] Liam: yes - our bench on similar workloads saw semantic deltas less than 1% on 4-bit quant for generative completions; for extraction tasks it's even lower. but we should run evals on your holdout prompts. we'll add that to the plan.

[04:20] Ethan: what's the fallback behaviour if a batch hits the latency SLO? do we drop or reroute?
[04:27] Maya: you can configure graceful fallback - route to a lower-latency variant (smaller model) or to Redwood Hosted with a strict latency SLA. we also support a circuit-breaker that returns a best-effort cached response.
[04:40] Sofia: hmm ok. I'd rather not degrade to host that sends data off-network - any privacy flags?
[04:46] Maya: understood. for NovaPay we can recommend Dedicated or Private deployments. Private keeps data on your VPC/onprem and uses your KMS. we'll send the Private deployment checklist.

[05:10] Liam: quick note about batching metrics - we instrument average batch size, wait time, fill ratio, and token efficiency. we'll send a dashboard with these metrics. the fill ratio moved from ~0.45 to 0.72 with the adaptive window which accounts for the throughput jump.

[05:35] Sofia: you mentioned queueing earlier - any recommendations on queue depth vs concurrency?
[05:38] Liam: yes - heuristically we set concurrency * avg_batch_size ~= target_inflight_requests. for your target 3k rps with avg tokens per request ~120, we set a target_inflight of ~150-200. with batch_size 16 that maps to concurrency cap ~12, but since internal worker parallelism differs, we used per-worker cap=32 and increased workers. it's a bit fuzzy because model latency per-token matters.

[06:10] Ethan: can you share the math spreadsheet?
[06:13] Maya: yes will attach the cost/workbook. link in chat after.

[06:25] Liam: also note warm KV cache gives big wins for chat-like flows. the continuous batching must respect KV cache locality - when cache hits are high you get a smaller token gen time which increases effective throughput; when cache miss rate is high you see lower fill ratio.

[07:00] Priya: ok show us the proposed run plan for the 4-hour benchmark.
[07:04] Liam: plan: spin up a dedicated test fleet mirroring your prod-ish request patterns, run 4 hours with increasing concurrency stages (stage 1: smoke, stage 2: 60% target, stage 3: 100% sustained), collect metrics: rps, p50/p95/p99, batch_size histograms, queue depth, fill ratio, error rates. we also record token-level cost. after run we'll do a 1-hour cooldown and then an analysis.
[07:40] Sofia: do you need us to provision infra or can you use our test cluster?
[07:44] Liam: prefer your test cluster to capture real network/infra behaviour; if you want we can run in Redwood Dedicated sandbox but that won't show your infra limits.

[08:00] Ethan: infra question - memory on our nodes is currently 320GB per machine; we saw OOMs with bigger batches when we tried 8-bit. any tips?
[08:08] Liam: a few: lower max_batch_size, enable model sharding or quantized kernels, or use sequence length capping. also consider moving to our Dedicated config with larger GPU memory. we'll put recommended node sizes in the doc.

[08:30] Maya: quick interjection - competition we've seen is Vertex and Anthropic offering fast inference; our edge is batching + tuning and private deployments.

[08:45] Sofia: anything in the perf deck about queue TTLs and why shorter TTL helped earlier?
[08:50] Liam: yes, page 6 covers TTL tradeoffs. shorter TTL avoids very long waits but reduces batch fill; longer TTL increases batch fill but hurts tail latency. we found 4-8s sweet spot for your workload.

[09:12] Maya: let's recap the immediate technical changes we applied since last week: 1) adaptive window for continuous batching, 2) KV cache enabled for repeated prompts, 3) concurrency cap tuning and queue TTL=6s. these moved throughput from 1.2k to 1.9k rps and reduced p95 from 320ms to 180ms in our tests.

[09:45] Sofia: nice. can you show logs where p95 dropped?
[09:49] Liam: yes - see the spreadsheet we linked; I'll also attach the timeline traces.

[10:05] Ethan: any concerns about autoscaler thrash when bursts are short?
[10:10] Liam: to avoid thrash we recommend rate-of-change gating: only scale up if queue depth > threshold for >30s and scale down with a cooldown of 3-5 minutes. Also prefer burst capacity by keeping one spare worker pool.

[10:35] Priya: what's the estimated cost delta if we move to Dedicated to hit 3k rps?
[10:41] Maya: rough estimate: servicing at 3k rps on Dedicated with recommended config is ~1.8-2.2x your current hosted bill (depends on tokens/use). we'll send a modeled worksheet.

[11:00] Sofia: can Redwood run a short A/B comparing quant variants? we want to see quality regressions.
[11:05] Liam: absolutely - we'll run evals against your holdout set as part of the 4-hour run. we'll include rouge/semantic similarity and an internal QC pass.

[11:25] Maya: any legal/compliance asks from your side before we run the benchmark in your cluster?
[11:30] Priya: just KMS integration and audit logs - Ethan will coordinate.
[11:34] Ethan: yep we'll need the audit log format and retention options.
[11:37] Maya: noted - I'll include audit options and SOC2 artifacts in the follow-up email.

[12:00] Sofia: last question - if the 4-hour run hits 3k with the quantized model but shows a 0.9% drop in extraction accuracy, do you have rollback/fast-fail mechanisms?
[12:10] Liam: yes - we do canary rollouts and automatic fallback routes. you can set an evaluation threshold and if quality dips beyond it we automatically route to the previous variant. that's in the rollout policies in the console.

[12:40] Maya: okay time for quick recap and owners. Liam will run the 4-hour benchmark, push config, and share results (due 6/25). Sofia will share traces (due 6/24). Maya will send pricing, SOC2, perf deck (due 6/24). We'll schedule the on-prem pilot if infra signoff is green.

[13:05] Priya: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[13:10] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up via email and update the CRM.
[13:15] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcript quality: there are some mis-transcriptions (KV cash, dedidcated) and occasional speaker overlap.
